title: Trump Flaunts Camaraderie With Xi and Putin but Has Little to Show for It
partialText: President Trump called Russia’s leader his “friend” and marveled at China’s warm welcome for his first-ever trilateral summit. But there were no breakthroughs on nuclear control, the war in Ukraine or A.I.

title: At Summit With Xi and Putin, Trump Seeks to Project Power Abroad While Sharing It at Home
partialText: Weakened by the midterm elections, President Trump offered hugs, arm pats and smiles to autocrats from Russia and China in contrast to the threats he is making to ascendant Democrats in Washington.

title: At APEC Summit, U.S., China and Russia Vow to Increase Oil Supply Amid Global Energy Transition
partialText: The United States, China and Russia agreed to boost the supply of refined petroleum products, as oil prices spike because of the Iran war.

title: The Bay Area Wonders: What Will Anthropic Workers Do With Their Wealth?
partialText: San Francisco isn’t preparing for an Anthropic shopping spree after employees gain newfound affluence from the company’s initial public offering.

title: Myanmar Committed Genocide Against the Rohingya, Top Global Court Finds
partialText: In a decision with potentially broad implications, the International Court of Justice found a state culpable of genocide for the first time.

title: Inside a Rohingya Camp After a Genocide Ruling
partialText: On Thursday, the International Court of Justice ruled that the atrocities against the Rohingya ethnic minority constituted a genocide waged by the Myanmar state. Before the decision, Hannah Beech, a New York Times correspondent, spent a week in the refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, home to at least 1.2 million Rohingya.

title: A Village Burned, Its People Killed or Exiled. A Court Ruled It Was Genocide.
partialText: Zammona’s erasure was part of a wider campaign of violence against Rohingya Muslims. An international court found that Myanmar was culpable for the atrocities.

title: Myanmar Genocide Ruling Sets Up Court Fight Over Israel and Gaza
partialText: The ruling by the International Court of Justice deals with issues relevant to the case brought against Israel alleging genocide in Gaza. Israel has rejected the charge.

title: Whatever You Thought Texas Was, It’s Bigger and Bluer Than That
partialText: After Democrats broke a decades-long Republican winning streak this month, Texans are reflecting on who gets to define the place they call home.

title: With Alaska’s Senate Vote Counted, What Comes Next in the Last Frontier?
partialText: The race is scheduled to be certified next week, but the Justice Department is investigating after Republicans lodged cheating allegations against the eventual winner, Mary Peltola.

title: Former Biden Chief, With Help From Alex Soros, Will Gather Aides of 2028 Hopefuls
partialText: Jen O’Malley Dillon, who led the former president’s last two White House bids, is inviting top Democratic operatives to a gathering funded in part by the megadonor Alex Soros.

title: Grand Theft Auto Used to Satirize American Life. Now We’ve Caught Up With It.
partialText: The G.T.A. series is more than just a crime simulator — it’s a cartoonish sendup of our country. What happens when reality outruns the joke?

title: Army Warns Iowa of Toxic Cloud as It Prepares to Blow Up Old Ammo
partialText: Friday’s explosion will dispose of unstable material used in detonators. A plume of dangerous lead dust could travel up to 60 miles, according to the latest Army estimate.

title: They’re Prepping for a World Where the Internet Doesn’t Work
partialText: “DoorDash is not an emergency plan.”

title: Intolerance of Uncertainty Is Rising in Young Adults
partialText: At a moment when technical glitches are stirring confusion and fear, a new analysis examines just how distressing uncertainty can feel.

title: What You Should Know About Downdetector Before the Next Big Tech Outage
partialText: The website has been checked and cited often during an unusually busy week of technology problems, though its operators acknowledge its limitations.

title: Trump Weighs New Strikes on Iran as Israel Presses for Action, Officials Say
partialText: Warnings that Iran is rebuilding its missile stockpile and advancing biological and chemical programs have divided the Trump administration.

title: Senate Republicans Block Bid to Rein in Trump on Iran War
partialText: In the first vote on the conflict since the midterm elections, most in the G.O.P. banded together against placing any limits on a conflict that voters repudiated at the polls.

title: At Brooklyn Compound, ICE Officers Are Training on Conducting Car Stops
partialText: Immigration and Customs Enforcement was ordered to expand training on traffic stops. The exercises come after a series of officer-involved shootings during President Trump’s immigration crackdown.

title: Fiona the Hippo, Star of Cincinnati Zoo and Beyond, Dies After Eating Child’s Hat
partialText: The beloved Nile hippopotamus became ill after eating a children’s hat that accidentally ended up in her enclosure.

title: After Bridge Attack, Putin Says He Will ‘Not Be Negotiating’ Ukraine Cease-Fire
partialText: The Russian leader invited European representatives to Moscow to discuss giving them a role in negotiations. It was unclear how serious the offer was.

title: Dutch and Austrian Embassies Are Damaged as Russian Drones Swarm Kyiv
partialText: Foreign ministers for Austria and the Netherlands said no one was harmed at their embassy compounds, and the European Union’s ambassador said a drone “exploded right above my head" by her hotel.

title: This Isn’t the Cyberapocalypse, but It Isn’t Great
partialText: A cybersecurity expert isn’t sold on the theory that there is a connection between the many recent digital failures and crashes.

title: ‘The Tuners’: The Hidden Contest at the International Chopin Piano Competition
partialText: In the shadows of one of the world’s most prestigious piano contests, the piano tuners are battling through their own competition.

title: California Storm Sweeps South, Prompting Some Evacuation Warnings in L.A.
partialText: A system that earlier flooded San Francisco was hitting Southern California on Thursday.
